quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Chemicals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Annual securities report, fiscal year April 2025 - March 2026: sales revenue fell 7.8% to JPY 1,668,754 million, mainly on lower selling prices following the decline in naphtha and other raw material prices and lower sales chiefly in Basic & Green Materials; core operating income fell 0.9% to JPY 100.0 billion on worse inventory valuation; operating income fell 5.8% to JPY 73.8 billion (including an impairment of the investment in an equity-method affiliate running a phenol business in China); net income attributable to owners of the parent rose 6.6% to JPY 34.4 billion. Overseas sales were JPY 864.7 billion, 51.8% of sales revenue. Segment sales: Life & Healthcare Solutions JPY 259,076 million (+2.9%), Mobility Solutions JPY 515,406 million (-7.2%; core operating income down on lower PP compound sales as OEMs cut output due to US tariffs, semiconductor supply shortages and a US aluminium plant fire), ICT Solutions JPY 279,436 million (+0.7%), Basic & Green Materials JPY 599,922 million (-15.5%; core operating loss widened to JPY 18.4 billion).
quarterly_data.figure: Sales revenue JPY 1,668,754 million (-7.8%); core operating income JPY 100.0 billion (-0.9%); net income attributable to owners JPY 34.4 billion (+6.6%); overseas sales 51.8%

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Chemicals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: ICT Solutions, fiscal year April 2025 - March 2026: sales revenue JPY 279,436 million (+0.7%), up despite the transfer of subsidiary shares; core operating income rose by JPY 10.2 billion to JPY 36.9 billion, mainly because sales of semiconductor and optical materials and of ICT films and sheets were firm on the recovery in semiconductor market demand; coating and functional materials sales were flat and nonwovens sales declined.
quarterly_data.figure: ICT Solutions sales revenue JPY 279,436 million (+0.7%); core operating income JPY 36.9 billion (up JPY 10.2 billion)

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Chemicals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Company forecast for the fiscal year April 2026 - March 2027 (the company's FY2026): sales revenue JPY 1.9 trillion (vs JPY 1,668.8 billion), core operating income JPY 105.0 billion (vs JPY 100.0 billion), operating income JPY 83.0 billion (vs JPY 73.8 billion), net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 45.0 billion (vs JPY 34.4 billion). Management states that instability in the Middle East following the US-Iran military clash keeps risks to energy supply and international logistics, and that domestic naphtha cracker utilisation remains low on weaker downstream demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Forecast: sales revenue JPY 1.9 trillion; core operating income JPY 105.0 billion; net income attributable to owners JPY 45.0 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Chemicals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: VISION 2030 financial targets (company fiscal years, which the report numbers by the year they begin in April): core operating income JPY 200.0 billion and net income attributable to owners JPY 110.0 billion in fiscal 2028, and JPY 250.0 billion and JPY 150.0 billion or more in fiscal 2030; ROE 10% or more (2028) and 13% or more (2030); ROIC 7% or more (2028) and 9% or more (2030). Fiscal April 2025 - March 2026 results fell short of plan: core operating income JPY 100.0 billion vs plan JPY 110.0 billion, net income JPY 34.4 billion vs plan JPY 55.0 billion, ROE 4.0% vs 6.4%, ROIC 4.5% vs 4.8%.
quarterly_data.figure: Core operating income targets JPY 200.0 billion (company fiscal 2028), JPY 250.0 billion (company fiscal 2030); ROE 13% or more by company fiscal 2030

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Chemicals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D spending in the fiscal year April 2025 - March 2026 was JPY 46.4 billion, of which ICT Solutions JPY 13.1 billion; in October 2025 a development department was set up in each growth-segment business sector. In semiconductors, against higher device performance and integration driven by generative AI and digitalisation, the company is developing EUV-exposure-related materials for advanced semiconductor manufacturing processes and film and sheet materials for ICT, and is working with outside partners on materials for next-generation semiconductor packaging; it is also developing AR optical technology.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 46.4 billion (ICT Solutions JPY 13.1 billion)

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Chemicals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management states that for ICROS Tape, used in semiconductor manufacturing processes where demand is growing for generative AI, the company added evaluation and prototyping functions at its group's Taiwan plant, alongside the Creating Integration Lab opened at Nagoya Works the previous year, to expand local development. For the AR/VR market it developed Diffrar resin wafers for AR-glass waveguides and succeeded in developing 12-inch optical resin wafers for AR glasses with refractive indices of 1.67 and 1.74, which it calls a world first (company research).
quarterly_data.figure: 12-inch AR optical resin wafers, refractive index 1.67 and 1.74

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Chemicals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management states that the semiconductor-centred ICT market is expected to grow over the medium to long term on DX and the spread of generative AI and is a key growth area, with focus fields semiconductors and packaging, imaging, battery materials and converting. Semiconductor and packaging products include Mitsui Pellicle photomask covers, high-purity silane and disilane gases for deposition, photoresist raw materials, ICROS Tape and heat-resistant release films; the plan is to expand overseas technical-service sites and analysis and evaluation functions, and to accelerate semiconductor-material R&D along the leading-edge technology roadmap through co-creation with customers and outside partners. In battery materials it aims to capture growth in industrial uses such as stationary power for data centres in addition to EVs.

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Chemicals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Basic & Green Materials restructuring: Idemitsu Kosan's Chiba ethylene cracker is to stop in July 2027 and the West Japan crackers of Asahi Kasei and Mitsubishi Chemical around fiscal 2030, with production consolidated into Mitsui Chemicals' facilities (final agreement with Idemitsu on December 19, 2025); Sumitomo Chemical's domestic polypropylene and LLDPE businesses are to be integrated into Prime Polymer in July 2026 (agreement December 24, 2025), after which Prime Polymer is owned 52% by Mitsui Chemicals, 28% by Idemitsu Kosan and 20% by Sumitomo Chemical; on December 15, 2025 the company decided to add 100 thousand tonnes of MDI capacity (to 710 thousand tonnes a year); it sold its entire 50% stake in the Shanghai phenol affiliate SSMC to Sinopec Shanghai Gaoqiao in December 2025; and since May 30, 2025 it has been studying a spin-off of the Basic & Green Materials business for reorganisation with other companies.
quarterly_data.figure: Prime Polymer ownership after integration: Mitsui Chemicals 52%, Idemitsu Kosan 28%, Sumitomo Chemical 20%

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Chemicals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio moves in Life & Healthcare: the tender offer for DNA Chip Research succeeded and it became a wholly owned subsidiary; on May 13, 2026 the board resolved that Mitsui Chemicals America will acquire Ultradent Products (dental whitening and restorative products, mainly in the Americas) through a new holding company, and the share transfer agreement was signed on June 12, 2026.
